questions.q: What is the main subject of this passage?
options: How a Soviet missile deployment in Cuba led to a tense US-Soviet standoff and its causes
How Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution against Batista reshaped US-Cuban trade relations
Why the United States placed Jupiter and Thor missiles in Turkey, Italy and England
How the failed Bay of Pigs invasion led Kennedy to win the 1960 election
questions.explain: The passage describes the 13-day confrontation over Soviet missiles in Cuba and the Cuba, US and Soviet background factors behind it.

questions.q: In which year did the US deploy Thor missiles in England under Project Emily?
questions.explain: The passage says that in 1959 the US deployed Thor nuclear missiles in England, known as Project Emily.

questions.q: What did Kennedy call his naval blockade of Cuba, and why?
options: A defense perimeter, to reassure the Soviet navy
A quarantine, to avoid the formal implications of a state of war
A patrol zone, to keep the United Nations involved
A shipping inspection, to satisfy Cuban exiles
questions.explain: Kennedy called it a quarantine so the US could avoid the formal implications of a state of war.

questions.q: What did the US secretly agree to do as part of the settlement?
options: Dismantle its offensive weapons in Turkey
Pay for UN inspections in Cuba
questions.explain: The passage says the United States secretly agreed to dismantle all offensive weapons it had deployed to Turkey.

questions.q: Why was the deal harmful to Khrushchev at home?
options: Kennedy refused to promise the United States would never invade Cuba again
The Politburo blamed him for losing the Soviet U-2 spy plane program
The secret deal made the Soviets look like they retreated from their own crisis
Castro publicly blamed him for losing the Soviet bombers and the alliance
questions.explain: The passage says the secret deal made the Soviets seem to retreat, embarrassing Khrushchev and contributing to his fall two years later.
